00 · Start here
A growth breakdown for Sorce
Why we made this

You built Sorce into Tinder for jobs: 850K+ people, 30M+ swipes since August 2024, and in David's words, "almost entirely from organic content". Your own TikToks show how: David's "6 months of applying to jobs and now I find this" passed 13.9M plays, and your 23 October update offers up to 40 applications a day.

This board is how we would add volume to all of that before the January job hunt. It is free, so take whatever is useful.

How to read this board
Use the list on the left, or press P to go frame by frame. On a phone, just scroll.
Creator cards: platform, followers and median views on recent videos.
Please note
Made by hypjam from public information, checked 25 Oct 2026. Nobody at Sorce asked for this, and it is not paid work. The creators named here have not been contacted and have no link to hypjam: they show the kind of people we would cast.
12 creators shortlisted, 4 scripts with 32 hooks, and a plan to put more real job seekers on camera before the January job hunt.

30M+: swipes since launch in August 2024
1M+: applications your AI agent has submitted for users

01 · Why UGC
Why creator videos work
Authenticity
People trust people
A founder saying "AI applies for you" is a claim. A laid-off engineer showing the interview email that came back is proof.
Show, do not tell
The swipe is the demo
Swipe right and the agent applies. Few products fit on a phone screen this fast: the whole idea is clear in the first two seconds.
Objections
Answer "will it apply to the wrong jobs?" out loud
A real person swiping left on what they would never take, and right on what they would, answers it before anyone asks.
Relatable
Everyone has a job-hunt story
Ghosted, 20 interviews, "still deciding". The jokes already travel on TikTok, and Sorce is the punchline that actually helps.
Fuel for ads
Your best ads come from creators
Videos that already work on TikTok can run as Spark Ads and Meta partnership ads, with 8 openings per script, so the budget follows what people actually watch.
Doesn't feel like an ad
Looks like a normal post
So people actually watch it instead of scrolling past. It is still labelled as an ad, it just does not feel like one.
02 · What we learned
Where Sorce is today
The product
Tinder for jobs. Upload a resume once, swipe right, and Sorce's AI agent applies on the company's own site: it fills every form, uploads documents, answers screening questions and writes cover letters. Swipe left to skip. Confirmations, interviews and offers land in an inbox inside the app.
The offer
Free swipes every day, on iPhone and iPad. Your 23 October update: up to 40 applications each day, and resumes from Google Drive, Photos, Files or a link. 4.7 stars from 36K ratings on the US App Store.
Your own channels
David's @careerdave: 13.9M plays on "6 months of applying to jobs and now I find this" and 9.2M on "Actually obsolete". Daniel's @okii.dan: 1.1M. Dada on X: 102K views on serving ~150k swipes in a single day.
Already in motion
  • David on 4 August: 800k+ users, "almost entirely from organic content".
  • Someone gets an interview through Sorce every 60 seconds, and 1,000+ users have landed jobs.
  • Users have interviewed at SpaceX, MongoDB, Neuralink, Jane Street and Scale AI.
  • The employer side has a waitlist open: people swipe right on a role, and an AI recruiter reviews every one.
What that tells us
Sorce travels when a real person shows the job hunt, then the swipe. Your biggest videos, from founders and from creators, all follow that pattern. What is missing is volume: many more faces, from more kinds of job seekers, every week.
The timing
January is the year's big job-search month: on Indeed, searches were up to 31% higher in January 2026 than in early December. Videos started in November have time to find what works before then.
Sources: sorce.jobs (home, download, employer and case study pages, llms.txt), the US App Store listing and its 23 Oct update, the YC company page and launch post, posts by @marvy_101 and @davidalade on X, TikTok video pages, and Indeed Hiring Lab (19 Feb 2026), all read 25 Oct 2026.

AI-tools creators

Job-search TikTok
The job hunt is its own genre: a "still deciding" interview skit from January has 13.2M plays, and a "28 and unemployed" POV from July has 3.7M.
The opening for Sorce
Most creator ads we found in the category run from career-advice accounts. Your biggest videos are different: a real job seeker, months of applying, then the swipe. That format is yours. The lane is more of those faces, in more job types, every week, with the winners running as ads.
Sources: Meta Ad Library (US, active ads, exact phrases aiapply.co, jobright.ai and simplify.jobs), TikTok bios and video pages, and @usesprout on TikTok, all read 25 Oct 2026.
04 · The objection
"Will it apply to the wrong jobs?": the objection to win
Before anyone lets an AI apply in their name, they ask two things: will it send something I would not, and will it actually get me interviews? The videos should answer both.
What you already promise
  • You stay in control: swipe right to apply, swipe left to skip
  • It reads your resume once, then fills every form and uploads every document
  • It answers screening questions and writes tailored cover letters
  • Defaults for questions you want answered the same way
  • Every confirmation, interview and offer shows up inside Sorce
The proof you already have
Someone gets an interview through Sorce every 60 seconds, 1,000+ users have landed jobs, and users have interviewed at companies like SpaceX, Neuralink and Jane Street.
The in-app inbox
Since January, every confirmation, interview and offer can be read inside Sorce. That screen is the most believable shot in any Sorce video: a real interview email, from a real swipe.
How we use it
Script A ends on the in-app inbox, days later. Script C has a recruiter swipe left out loud and say why. Scripts B and D swipe left as often as right, so viewers see the choice stays theirs.
On camera
Resumes, emails and phone numbers are blurred. Interview emails show the company, never a recruiter's name or address. Only jobs the creator would really take get a right swipe.
What creators never say
No promised number of interviews or offers. No "guaranteed job" and no "recruiters can't tell". Nothing your own pages do not say Sorce does.
05 · Audience
Who to sell to first
Start here
New grads and students
Your launch post says a CS student applies to 100 to 200 internships. Applying in volume is their whole autumn, and they film it. Formats A and B.
Start here
People who were laid off
Ex-Google engineers, law grads and marketers starting over already post their search every week. The swipe and the in-app inbox are their next update. Format A.
Broadest reach
Everyone tired of the job hunt
Ghosted, "still deciding", the same form for the 80th time. The jokes already travel, and Sorce is the punchline that helps. Format B.
Switchers
Teachers, nurses and anyone starting over
Sorce covers the whole spectrum, from retail and healthcare to senior roles. Switchers search for new job titles, which makes great list videos. Formats C and D.
Where we would start
New grads and laid-off professionals first. Both already film their search every week, both apply to dozens of roles, and the swipe is the easiest product moment in the category to show.
06 · The moment
The January job hunt starts in November
Every January, job searches surge: on Indeed they were up to 31% higher in January 2026 than in early December. Hooks tested in November are proven by then.
Now to Thanksgiving (26 Nov)
Swipe sessions and Tinder-for-jobs skits (Scripts A and B) go live, and the best openings start running as ads.
December
Budget moves to the winning hooks. "So, how's the job search going?" season at family dinners, and year-end recaps of every application sent.
January
The winners run at full volume for the new-year surge, plus new creators for switchers: teachers, nurses and people starting over (Script D).
What this needs from you
  • A short list of what creators can show today: the swipe, the applications list, the in-app inbox
  • A link or code per creator
  • Dada, Daniel or David for a founder cut of Script A, if you want it
Why start now
Indeed's data shows people pause their searches over the holidays, then return in force in January. Videos made now are tested and cut by the time they do.
07 · The first month
Your first four weeks
Week 1 · 2-8 Nov
You approve the shortlist and the 4 formats. We sign creators and send each one a script with 8 hooks. They upload a resume and start swiping on their own accounts.
Week 2 · 9-15 Nov
First videos come in, and we review each within 48 hours. Swipe sessions and job-hunt skits first.
Week 3 · 16-22 Nov
First videos go live. The best openings start as TikTok Spark Ads and Meta partnership ads, each with its creator's own link.
Week 4 · 23-29 Nov
Results review together: downloads by creator and by ad, and the plan for December and the January surge.
If it is a yes this week
Agreement signed and creators swiping on Sorce by Friday. First videos live within 14 days of the scripts being signed off.
08 · Formats
Four formats for Sorce
A · Downloads
I let AI apply to jobs for me
A real job seeker films one week: a swipe session on the commute, then the in-app inbox a few days later. Cut into 15 and 30 second ads that point at the App Store.
your "6 months of applying", 13.9M ↗"how am i just now finding this", 9.5M ↗
B · Reach
Tinder, but for jobs
A comedy creator swipes on jobs like dating profiles: "remote, great team, loves spreadsheets". Right swipe, and the agent applies. If a real interview comes back, that is the match.
the "still deciding" skit, 13.2M ↗"28 and unemployed", 3.7M ↗
C · Trust
A recruiter swipes for you
A recruiter or career coach swipes through real roles out loud: left on this one and why, right on that one. Then opens the applications list. It answers "will it apply to the wrong jobs?" by doing it.
@teets.x recruiter advice, 1.1M ↗@timmadden83 interview answers, 190K ↗
D · Saves
5 jobs you can get with your experience
A switcher lists 5 job titles people like them can apply for, searches each one in Sorce and swipes. Built to be saved and sent to a friend.
@briahnanicoleb teacher jobs, 437K ↗@sabelpop marketing jobs, 504K ↗
In every video
1 A real job seeker using Sorce with their own resume, never a staged review. 2 The swipe on screen in the first 2 seconds. 3 One payoff on screen: applied, or a real interview email if one came. 4 Personal details blurred: names, emails, phone numbers. 5 "Ad | Paid partnership" on screen plus the platform label.

10 · Script A
Script A: I let AI apply to jobs for me
The brief

Where: TikTok and Instagram Reels on the creator's own account, then the best cut as TikTok Spark Ads and Meta partnership ads to the App Store (15s and 30s)

Length: 38-42s master. 30s cut: shots 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 and 8. 15s cut: shots 1, 3, 6 and 8.

Goal: Downloads from people actively job hunting: new grads and laid-off professionals

Who films it: An 18+ creator who is really job hunting (a new grad, or someone laid off) and has used Sorce with their own resume for a week before filming. Founder version: Dada, Daniel or David, swiping as a demo in their own words. Filmed on a phone: the commute or the couch, then the same spot a few days later.

8 hooks to test (on screen, then spoken)
  1. [6] months of applying to jobs and now I find this[Six] months of applying to jobs by hand, and now I find this. [only if true]
  2. I let an AI apply to jobs for me for a weekFor one week, I'm letting an AI apply to jobs for me. Here's what came back.
  3. Swipe right = it applies for meSwipe right, and it applies for me. On the company's own site.
  4. I applied to [30] jobs before my coffee got coldI just applied to [thirty] jobs before my coffee got cold.
  5. Typing my name into one more application form? No.If I type my name into one more application form, I'm done. So I tried this.
  6. POV: you got tired of filling out 100s of applicationsThis is for everyone who's tired of filling out hundreds of applications.
  7. Day [1] of letting AI do my job applicationsDay [one] of letting AI do my job applications. Let's see what happens.
  8. Laid off [8] weeks ago. Here's my new system.I was laid off [eight] weeks ago, and this is my new system for applying. [only if true]

Rules for this video

'Ad | Paid partnership with Sorce' on screen for the whole video, said in the first 5 seconds, and the platform's paid-partnership label on. Founder version: 'Ad | I'm a co-founder of Sorce', said in the first 5 seconds. Only real swipes on jobs the creator would take, with their own resume. Nothing staged or mocked up. Results shown exactly as they happened. No promised number of interviews or offers. If nothing came back, the video says so. Personal details blurred: the creator's email, phone and address, and any recruiter's name or email. Only claims from Sorce's own pages: swipe right to apply, left to skip; it fills forms, uploads documents, answers screening questions and writes cover letters; free swipes every day; interviews and offers in the app.

Why it should convert
It shows the whole promise in one week instead of a feature list, and it follows the format behind David's 13.9M video: months of applying, then the swipe. The in-app inbox is the proof a 15 second ad needs.

Product moment and call to action

Sorce's search is on screen from 0:00. Every title on the list is searched and swiped in the app, so the product is in every beat; shot 5 shows a real right swipe.

CTA: Save the list, then download Sorce from the link in bio.

Caption
5 jobs you can get with your teaching experience (i swiped on all of them in sorce). save this for later #ad #careerchange #teachertok #sorce
Rules for this video

'Ad | Paid partnership with Sorce' on screen for the whole video, said in the first 5 seconds, and the platform's paid-partnership label on. Job titles and roles are real and appear exactly as they do in the app on the day. No salary or hiring claims unless the job card shows them. Right swipes only on jobs the creator would really take. Only claims from Sorce's own pages, and no promised interviews or offers.

Why it should convert
List videos get saved and shared, and switchers search for new job titles all the time. Bri's "what jobs can teachers even apply for?" has passed 436K plays since 5 October; doing the same list inside Sorce turns advice into a download.

16 · Ads
How the paid ads would run
1 · Film
Each script is shot once, with 8 different openings.
→
2 · Launch
Each opening runs as its own ad, from the creator's handle as a partnership ad.
→
3 · Read
After a few days we compare cost per download and how many people watch past 3 seconds.
4 · Cut
The weakest openings switch off and the budget moves to the best two.
→
5 · Remix
Winning hooks get new bodies and new creators.
→
6 · Refresh
New creator videos every week, so the ads never go stale.
Where the ads point
Your App Store page, through one link per creator, so every download traces back to the video that drove it. The same videos run as TikTok Spark Ads and Meta partnership ads.
Why partnership ads
Ads that run from a creator's own handle look like that creator's post, not a brand ad. That is the format these videos are built for.
What we would need
Access to your TikTok and Meta ad accounts (or we run them from ours), downloads by link, and a weekly look at the numbers.
17 · Process
How a campaign runs, step by step
1 · Brief
You tell us the goal, the audience and what can and can't be said about Sorce.
→
2 · Cast
We shortlist creators by niche, location and median views. You pick.
→
3 · Offer
We send each creator the brief, the dates and the rate.
4 · Sign
A written agreement with every creator, covering usage and disclosure.
→
5 · Scripts
One per format: 8 hooks, a shot list, screens to record and a caption.
→
6 · Film and upload
Creators film on their phones and upload to a private folder only we see.
7 · Review
We check every video within 48 hours. Nothing posts unapproved.
→
8 · Post
On the creator's own account, with the ad disclosure and the paid-partnership label.
→
9 · Pay and report
Creators paid within 7 days of going live. You get a report every Monday.
Where creators talk to us
One hypjam Discord for every creator. Each campaign gets a private channel group for chat, scripts and posted links that only its creators and your team can see.
Accounts
Each signed creator uploads their own resume and uses Sorce for a week before filming. Anything readable on screen is theirs, or blurred.
18 · Reporting
What we report, and when
Every video
Views, how many people stay past 3 seconds, average watch time, saves, shares and comments.
Every creator link
A tracking link for each creator, so downloads trace back to the video that drove them.
Every Monday
A short report: every video, the hooks that won, downloads by creator, and what we change next.
Every month
A review call: spend, downloads, cost per result on anything run as an ad, and the plan for next month.
19 · Rules
Rules we never break
Disclosure
"Ad | Paid partnership with Sorce" on screen, said in the first seconds, and the platform's paid-partnership label on. That is what the FTC asks for.
Who films
Adults only (18+). Creators use Sorce themselves before they talk about it.
What gets said
Nothing your own pages do not say Sorce does. No invented numbers. We never pay for a positive opinion, only for the video.
Applications on camera
Creators only swipe right on jobs they would really take. Resumes, emails, phone numbers and any recruiter's name are blurred.
No promised results
Nobody promises interviews, offers or reply rates. Creators show what happened to them, and only what your own pages say Sorce does.
How we run it
Every video reviewed within 48 hours before it posts. Creators paid within 7 days of going live.
